content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: A package needs reproducible dependencies, namespace/documentation, tests and checks before release. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Describe which check would detect an example, documentation or dependency problem. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Package Testing and Development Workflow
content_blocks.code:
# Lesson 213: Package Testing and Development Workflow
example_result <- 5 * 2
stopifnot(example_result == 10)
"check passed"
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: A successful assertion is useful evidence for one condition only; add negative and boundary tests too. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For package testing and development workflow, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Relying on a package attached only in the interactive workspace.
common_mistakes.why: A clean session may not have that dependency attached or installed.
common_mistakes.fix: Declare imports and test package functions from a fresh R session.

common_mistakes.problem: Publishing examples without running their tests or checks.
common_mistakes.why: Documentation can be stale and examples can fail on a clean machine.
common_mistakes.fix: Run package tests and R CMD check under the supported R version.

common_mistakes.problem: Leaving dependencies and version assumptions undocumented.
common_mistakes.why: Users may not be able to reproduce the package behavior.
